This price was implied by faith that Guyana and the Permian would lift volumes and net margins as advanced technologies reshaped recovery efficiency and the cost base. That combination, alongside record output in Guyana and the Permian, aligned more closely with the optimistic thesis. At the same time, geopolitical risks and derivative losses reminded investors that the cautious story had not disappeared. The lesson is simple. title: Exxon earnings: $19B cash haul comes with a catch - TradingView
content: ExxonMobil’s (XOM) latest earnings give investors something more useful than another headline about soaring oil profits: a test of how much cash the business can generate – and how much shareholders should expect to keep receiving. The energy giant reported third-quarter net income of $15.4 billion on October 30, with adjusted earnings of $4.23 per share beating the $4.08 LSEG consensus. Refining strength helped drive the result, as disruptions to global fuel supplies boosted margins. But the investment question extends beyond this quarter’s windfall: what survives when those conditions ease? Refining reveals why Exxon is more than an oil-price bet Exxon’s Energy Products segment earned $7.17 billion, edging past the $7.09 billion generated by its upstream business. Compared with Q2, fuel-making profits increased while upstream earnings declined. That divergence illustrates the value of owning businesses across the energy supply chain. For investors, crude prices alone therefore offer an incomplete guide to Exxon’s prospects. Refiners earn money from the spread between feedstock costs and finished-fuel prices; that spread can strengthen even when oil-production earnings weaken. Integration provides another source of earnings, but unusually favorable refining conditions can also flatter consolidated profitability. Investors assessing future earnings should watch diesel margins alongside crude prices, rather than assume every business will keep contributing at today’s pace. XOM’s cash cushion is substantial – but timing helped Exxon generated $19.1 billion in free cash flow and distributed $9.4 billion through dividends and buybacks. Its reported cash generation therefore covered those payments roughly twice over, leaving considerable financial flexibility. However, working-capital movements contributed approximately $2.2 billion to operating cash flow. Excluding those movements, operating cash flow fell to $23.4 billion from $25.7 billion in the preceding quarter, even as the headline measure increased. That distinction matters because inventory, receivables and payment timing can shift cash between reporting periods without representing a lasting improvement in earning power. Shareholders still received strong cash backing for their payouts. But annualizing the headline free-cash-flow figure would risk treating a favorable quarterly movement as recurring income. The more revealing test is cash generation across several quarters, after investment needs and working-capital swings. Exxon also announced $20 billion of share repurchases for 2027, subject to reasonable market conditions. The qualification deserves attention: it preserves management’s ability to respond if the operating environment deteriorates. Buybacks can increase remaining shareholders’ ownership and support per-share earnings, but their investment value depends on the price paid and the cash available through the cycle. A large authorization alone cannot establish that shares are cheap. For prospective buyers, the strongest takeaway is Exxon’s capacity to convert favorable markets into financial flexibility. The unresolved question is how much of that capacity persists under more ordinary conditions. Friday’s results make cash coverage, refining profitability and capital allocation the measures to watch next. Those will help distinguish a stronger underlying business from a particularly lucrative quarter. Select market data provided by ICE Data Services. Select reference data provided by FactSet. title: Exxon CEO Says Diesel Is The ‘Key Crunch Point’ In Global Fuel Shortage – Oil Giant To Continue Investing ‘Several Billion Dollars’ In Refineries - TradingView
content: ExxonMobil (XOM) CEO Darren Woods said on Friday that global diesel supplies remain under severe pressure as geopolitical conflicts disrupt refining operations and fuel shipments, driving prices higher. In an interview with CNBC, Woods said Exxon is operating its refineries at record levels to maximize fuel production amid tight global supplies. “And frankly, diesel is the key crunch point here, because it is so critical to economic growth. Demand for diesel remains high despite capacity,” Woods said, adding that Exxon has focused heavily on maximizing refinery throughput, with refineries operating at record utilization levels and diesel yields reaching record highs. XOM shares were up 1.9% at the time of writing, hitting an all-time high. Woods pointed to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz amid the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, along with Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries, as major disruptions to global fuel supplies. “Refining capacity is very tight today,” Woods said, adding that while crude oil supplies have somewhat recovered, refining capacity remains the biggest constraint, limiting the availability of diesel and other refined products. Woods said Exxon will continue to invest “several billion dollars” in refineries to get more diesel out into the marketplace. “Our expectation is, we’re going to increase distillate throughput by about 100,000 barrels a day, as we go forward,” Woods said. Exxon reported third-quarter (Q3) revenue of $113.16 billion, beating Wall Street estimates of $105.24 billion, according to Fiscal.ai. content: ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation XOM reported third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of $4.23 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.90 per share by 8.5%. The bottom line increased from the year-ago figure of $1.88 per share. Revenues of $113.16 billion topped the consensus estimate of $103 billion by 9.9% and increased 32.7% year over year from $85.29 billion. GAAP earnings per share (EPS) rose to $3.72 from $1.76 in the year-ago quarter. The strong results were primarily driven by record refining margins, operational efficiency and optimization activities. Higher profitability was supported by strong Energy Products performance despite disruptions in Middle East production. Upstream production totaled 4,496 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day (Mboe/d). ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation Quote ExxonMobil's Energy Products segment generated adjusted earnings of $9.05 billion in the third quarter of 2026. The segment benefited from exceptionally strong refining margins as global supply disruptions constrained the availability of gasoline, diesel and other refined products. Refining capacity disruptions in Russia and the Middle East tightened product markets, supporting stronger margins. XOM's global refining network and optimization capabilities helped capture favorable market conditions. The company achieved record global diesel yields and North American diesel volumes during the first nine months of 2026. Energy Products sales totaled 5,753 thousand barrels per day (Mbd) in third-quarter. Global refinery throughput reached 3,735 Mbd, supported by strong utilization across the company's refining network. XOM's Upstream segment reported adjusted earnings of $7.31 billion in the third quarter. Higher commodity prices supported earnings, while production disruptions in the Middle East and increased depreciation associated with advantaged investments weighed on performance. The company continued benefiting from production growth in Guyana and the Permian Basin. Permian output remained above 1.8 MMboe/d, supported by technology-driven improvements in recovery and capital efficiency. Middle East disruptions constrained production availability. The company reported regional production of approximately 550 Mboe/d, while shipping restrictions delayed recognition of certain sales and revenues in the UAE. XOM Sees Support From Chemical & Specialty Products ExxonMobil's Chemical Products segment generated adjusted earnings of $725 million during the quarter. Record operational reliability and North American feedstock advantages supported profitability, although weaker chemical margins presented challenges. Chemical Products sales totaled 4,888 thousand metric tons. Strong operational execution and increased demand for high-value products in Asia Pacific supported the business despite elevated regional product availability and higher feedstock costs. Specialty Products contributed adjusted earnings of $1.28 billion, supported by favorable basestock margins. Sales volumes totaled 1,737 thousand metric tons, while the company's focus on differentiated products and structural cost reductions supported profitability. ExxonMobil's Expenses Rise Despite Efficiency Gains XOM's total costs and other deductions increased 23.6% to $91.93 billion from $74.36 billion. Crude oil and product purchases rose 37.1% to $65.72 billion, reflecting the higher cost of materials purchased during the quarter. Production and manufacturing expenses increased 11.1% to $11.22 billion from $10.09 billion. Depreciation and depletion expenses rose 5.1% to $6.80 billion, reflecting the impact of the company's expanding asset base and investments. Selling, general and administrative expenses declined 11.7% to $2.68 billion from $3.03 billion, providing some cost relief. ExxonMobil's cumulative structural cost savings have reached $16.9 billion since 2019, reflecting continued efforts to improve operational efficiency. ExxonMobil's income before taxes increased 94.3% to $21.24 billion from $10.93 billion. The improvement reflected stronger revenue generation and favorable refining conditions, which more than offset increased operating expenses. Income tax expenses rose 64.8% to $5.21 billion from $3.16 billion, reflecting higher taxable earnings. Despite the increased tax burden, net income attributable to ExxonMobil surged 104.2% to $15.41 billion from $7.55 billion in the year-ago quarter. The company's overall profitability benefited from its integrated operating model, which helped capture stronger refining margins amid global supply constraints. Free cash flow totaled $19.11 billion, reflecting cash generation after investments and other cash-flow adjustments. The company returned $9.4 billion to shareholders, including $4.3 billion in dividends and $5.1 billion in share repurchases. Cash capital expenditures totaled $7 billion, reflecting continued investments in advantaged projects and long-term production capacity. Middle East disruptions are expected to keep approximately 350 Mboe/d offline. Higher scheduled maintenance in Product Solutions could affect performance. Author:

                      Updated on: 2026-10-30 ExxonMobil (NYSE: XOM) heads into its third-quarter 2026 earnings release, with refining margins expected to deliver its largest positive contribution to earnings. Its October 16 filing estimates a $4.5 billion improvement in Energy Products margins versus the second quarter, offset by a $1.3 billion earnings drag from lower liquids prices. The reported change in company-wide profitability will depend on the refining benefit and other operating and accounting effects. Consensus forecasts put earnings at $4.03 per share and revenue at $106.02 billion, up from $1.88 and $85.29 billion a year earlier. XOM closed at $183.29 on October 29, following a rally. ExxonMobil had not published its Q3 results on the investor-relations page when checked, so company disclosures and forecasts remain separate. Earnings expectations: Q3 consensus forecasts stand at $4.03 per share and $106.02 billion in revenue, both estimates, not reported results. Refining profitability: ExxonMobil estimates a $4.5 billion quarter-on-quarter improvement in Energy Products margins, its largest favourable disclosed market factor. Upstream pressure: Lower liquids prices are expected to reduce upstream earnings by $1.3 billion, partly offset by $300 million from natural gas prices. Shareholder returns: Q2 free cash flow of $17.2 billion covered $9.4 billion of dividends and repurchases, providing a benchmark for Q3. XOM stock: Shares rallied ahead of the results, while recurring profitability and cash generation remain measures of operating performance. Consensus forecasts imply earnings-per-share growth of about 114% versus the prior year and revenue growth of roughly 24%. Those rates are calculations based on the forecast comparison figures, not ExxonMobil’s own Q3 guidance. The EPS growth comparison assumes the forecast and year-earlier figures use consistent accounting measures. The $4.03 estimate would represent a 14.5% increase from Q2 adjusted earnings per share of $3.52, provided the forecast and reported measures are comparable. ExxonMobil reported $14.5 billion in Q2 GAAP profit and $14.7 billion in adjusted earnings, excluding specified non-operational items and estimated timing effects. The two measures distinguish reported profitability from earnings adjusted for those items. ExxonMobil’s Energy Products business refines crude oil and sells products such as gasoline and diesel, which have different pricing dynamics. Refining margins improve when product prices rise relative to feedstock and processing costs, allowing the business to earn more from its output. Lower crude realisations can reduce upstream earnings while supporting parts of the refining business during the same quarter. The company’s filing estimates a $4.5 billion benefit from Energy Products margins, offset by a $600 million decline from Chemical Products margins and supplemented by a $500 million improvement in Speciality Products margins. Together, these changes produce an estimated $4.4 billion favourable margin effect across the three businesses, before other operating and accounting factors. The calculation measures selected quarter-over-quarter changes rather than additional net profit because it must also include commodity-price movements, operational costs, and other adjustments. Source: ExxonMobil’s October 16 Form 8-K; selected estimated drivers, not Q3 results. The preliminary filing separately identifies approximately $2.5 billion in unfavourable Q3 timing effects, including $1.9 billion assigned to Energy Products. Such effects largely arise when derivatives are valued before the related physical commodity transactions appear in earnings, potentially creating temporary differences between accounting results and commercial performance. Q2 also contained timing adjustments, so the full Q3 amount does not represent a new quarter-over-quarter loss without comparing the corresponding adjustments in both periods. ExxonMobil reported Q2 upstream earnings of $7.9 billion under GAAP and $9.2 billion on an adjusted basis, a $1.3 billion difference between the two profitability measures. Permian output exceeded 1.8 million oil-equivalent barrels per day, while total company production averaged 4.514 million barrels of oil equivalent per day. Regional production growth does not necessarily translate into a proportional increase in total company output. For Q3, the filing estimates that lower liquids prices will reduce upstream earnings by $1.3 billion and higher natural gas prices will add $300 million. It also lists a $900 million unfavourable change from other upstream factors such as entitlements, sales timing and tax impacts. These estimates show that upstream profitability depends on realised selling prices and other financial effects alongside production volumes. Guyana offers a separate source of prospective growth, with ExxonMobil’s fifth offshore production vessel scheduled to start up in Q4, as announced in its Q2 update. The project is expected to add 250,000 barrels per day of production capacity, although capacity is not the same as immediate realised output. Start-up timing and operating costs will determine its near-term contribution, while oil prices will influence the revenue earned on additional barrels. It returned $4.3 billion in dividends and $5.1 billion through share repurchases, for combined shareholder distributions of $9.4 billion. Q3 cash flow will show whether additional refining earnings translated into greater financial flexibility after capital spending. Published analyst consensus targets of $167.70 and $179.41 both sit below the $183.29 October 29 close, based on different analyst samples and reporting dates. These targets reflect analysts’ valuation estimates rather than a determination of ExxonMobil’s intrinsic value. The company’s recurring earnings capacity provides a basis for assessing its valuation under less favourable energy-market conditions. Production efficiency, lower structural costs and additional profitable output could support future earnings even if refining margins retreat from elevated levels. Without corresponding improvements in these areas, earnings from elevated refining margins may not hold up in subsequent quarters. Overall, ExxonMobil’s preliminary figures show a substantial refining benefit, but the disclosed offsets prevent a reliable company-wide earnings forecast based on that margin improvement alone. Its Q2 cash generation and expanding production assets provide clear benchmarks for assessing the next set of results. The October 30 release will establish whether the expected financial improvements translated into stronger adjusted earnings, segment profitability and free cash flow. title: Chevron and Exxon hit all-time highs as refining profits soar in reaction to Iran and Ukraine wars - CNBC
content:
Chevron and ExxonMobil on Friday reported profits that soared in the third quarter, as their U.S. refineries ramped up production to full capacity to take advantage of high diesel fuel prices. Chevron shares are up nearly 2% while Exxon is more than 1% higher. Both touched all-time highs Friday. The world is facing a fuel crisis as Ukraine, Iran and Houthi militants attack refineries in Russia and the Middle East, reducing global capacity by millions of barrels per day. Importers have increasingly turned to U.S. Gulf Coast refineries for diesel supplies as a consequence. ExxonMobil’s profits doubled to $15.4 billion, or $3.72 a share, compared to $7.5 billion, or $1.76 a share, in the same period in 2025. When adjusted for one-time items, it posted earnings of $4.23 a share, soundly beating Wall Street’s expectations. “Refining capacity is very tight today,” Exxon CEO Darren Woods told CNBC in an interview. “Frankly, diesel is the key crunch point here because it is so critical to economic growth [with] very inelastic demand.” U.S. diesel stood at a national average of $6.32 per gallon on Friday, an increase of more than 70% compared to the same period last year, according to AAA. Prices in the U.S. hit a record high in September. Chevron’s net income surged nearly 200% to $9.9 billion, or $5.06 a share, compared to $3.5 billion, or $1.82 a share, in the same period last year. When adjusted for one-time items, it reported earnings of $5.28 per share, also beating the Street’s expectations of $4.89. “The system is under stress,” Chevron CEO Mike Wirth told CNBC in an interview. “We remain in an environment that is fairly fragile.” Here’s what Chevron and Exxon earned, compared with estimates from analysts polled by LSEG: High profits from the largest oil companies at a time of war is politically controversial. President Donald Trump said in August that Chevron and Exxon “were making too much money based on a shortage.” The supply disruption began in March after the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran. Profits from Chevron’s refining division surged more than 300% to $4.9 billion compared to $1.1 billion in the same period in 2025. Its oil and gas production generated earnings of $5.7 billion, up 70% from $3.3 billion in the year-ago period. Chevron’s U.S. refineries processed record amounts of crude oil at just above 1 million barrels per day, as the facilities ran at 98% capacity. Diesel and jet fuel yields rose more than 10%, Wirth said. Exxon’s refining division generated profits of about $7.2 billion in the quarter, outpacing its production business’ earnings of about $7.1 billion. Its refining profits have surged nearly 200% to $11.4 billion so far this year compared to $4 billion during the first nine months of 2025. Exxon’s Gulf Coast refineries operated at 100% capacity utilization. Those refineries produced “record volumes of diesel” in the quarter, Woods said. Chevron’s oil and gas production actually declined slightly to 3.9 million barrels per day compared to about 4 million bpd in the same period last year. The decline was in its international segment due in part to the conflict in the Middle East, while output was largely flat in the U.S. year over year. Exxon has produced about 4.5 million bpd this year, a more than 2% decline from nearly 4.7 million during the first nine months of 2025. Got a confidential news tip? We want to hear from you.                         Patricia Miller ExxonMobil Q3 earnings beat estimates as refining profit more than doubled, offsetting lower upstream results. It also set $20 billion of 2027 share buybacks. ExxonMobil's third-quarter beat rested mainly on refining, where war-related fuel shortages lifted margins and more than doubled Energy Products earnings, offsetting weaker oil and gas production profit as prices fell. The company kept 2027 buybacks at $20 billion and extended its dividend streak, while citing geopolitical, market and regulatory conditions as risks to its plans. ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation (NYSE: XOM) reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $4.23 per share on Friday, ahead of the $4.08 analysts had expected, according to LSEG data, as refining profit more than doubled from the second quarter and offset weaker results from oil and gas production. Adjusted earnings rose to $17.5 billion from $14.7 billion in the second quarter, above the $16.6 billion analysts had forecast. Net income under U.S. GAAP was $15.4 billion, or $3.72 per share, compared with $14.5 billion, or $3.48 per share, three months earlier. The results come as fighting in the Middle East, including the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, and Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries have knocked out fuel-making capacity and caused global diesel shortages. Higher fuel prices have lifted profits across Western oil majors, and Shell and TotalEnergies also reported higher-than-expected earnings on Thursday. "Advantaged investments, technology, and $16.9 billion in structural cost savings since 2019 are expanding our earnings power. These are lasting improvements, not simply the result of favorable prices and margins," Darren Woods, ExxonMobil chairman and chief executive officer, said in the earnings release. Adjusted earnings from Energy Products, the segment that includes refining, rose to $9.1 billion from $4.1 billion in the second quarter. The company attributed the gain to higher margins and strong operations, including 100% crude unit utilization at its U.S. Gulf Coast refineries, meaning they processed crude at full capacity. ExxonMobil said Gulf Coast diesel output was the second-highest on record. It also reported record year-to-date refining performance, including its highest global diesel yield and highest North American diesel volumes, based on internal data available from 2014. Woods pointed to earlier spending on distillates, the fuel category that includes diesel. "On the U.S. Gulf Coast, investments such as our Beaumont refinery expansion have contributed to an increase in our distillate production by approximately 40% since 2019," he said. Adjusted Upstream earnings, which come from oil and gas production, fell to $7.3 billion from $9.2 billion. The company cited lower prices and an accelerated Guyana entitlement impact, which affects the share of output it receives under its contract there. Production was roughly flat at about 4.5 million barrels of oil equivalent per day. ExxonMobil has a higher share of production in the Middle East than its rivals. Its year-to-date results include $921 million of Middle East impacts, which the company excluded from adjusted earnings. During the quarter, the company took over as operator of the Papua LNG project in Papua New Guinea and reached agreements to increase its working interests to 34% in Papua LNG and 50% in Rovuma LNG in Mozambique, where it was already the operator. Last month it signed an agreement to explore for and produce shale in Azerbaijan, and it has held talks about a possible return to Venezuela. Chemical Products adjusted earnings fell to $725 million from $1.2 billion as margins declined. Specialty Products rose to $1.3 billion from $969 million on higher basestock margins, the base oils used to make lubricants. The gap between reported and adjusted earnings mainly reflects $2.5 billion of negative timing effects, which the company said relate largely to derivatives valued at period-end prices before the linked physical shipments are booked. title: Exxon (XOM) and Chevron (CVX) cancel plans for their executives to travel to the UAE’s ADIPEC oil conference next week on security grounds, according to reports, citing sources - Newsquawk
content: Exxon (XOM) and Chevron (CVX) cancel plans for their executives to travel to the UAE’s ADIPEC oil conference next week on security grounds, according to reports, citing sources. Cancellations of this kind are a standard tell when corporate security teams assess elevated regional risk: major oil companies pulled executives and staff travel to Gulf events during past episodes of US-Iran tension, tanker incidents, and threats to regional energy infrastructure, typically well before any disruption materialised. The signal lies in who is acting rather than what is said publicly: in-house risk assessments at the supermajors are conservative by design, and a withdrawal on security grounds implies a live threat picture rather than diplomatic atmospherics. The relevant mechanism for crude is the risk premium channel, with past episodes of this type tending to firm prompt spreads and raise the cost of freight and insurance for Gulf loadings even where physical flows were uninterrupted. The distinction that matters is whether the concern is a general regional posture, in which case the premium fades as headlines do, or whether it precedes an actual incident, in which case the market reprices around specific chokepoints and export terminals. Worth watching are parallel cancellations by other firms or governments, official travel advisories for the region, and any guidance from the companies themselves, since a lone cancellation reads differently from a coordinated pullback. title: Exxon Mobil Holdings (XOM) Q1 2026 Earnings Call Transcript - Fortune
content:
Jim ChapmanGood morning, everyone. Welcome to ExxonMobil's earnings call. Today's call is being recorded. We appreciate you joining us. I'm Jim Chapman and I'm joined by Darren Woods, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, and Neil Hansen, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. This quarter's presentation and prerecorded remarks are available on the investors section of our website. They're meant to accompany this quarter's earnings release, which is posted in the same location. During today's presentation, we'll make forward-looking remarks, including comments on our long-term plans, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please read our cautionary statement on slide two. You can find more information on the risks and uncertainties that apply to any forward-looking statements in our SEC filings on our website. We also provide supplemental information at the end of our earnings slides, which are also posted on our website. Now I'll turn it over to Darren for opening remarks. Darren WoodsGood morning, and thank you for joining us. Let me begin by recognizing the impact of the conflict in the Middle East on our colleagues and partners in the region. We've been in close contact with our regional partners, as well as with companies and countries we have worked with for many years. We are proud to stand beside them during these very difficult times. While the financial impact in the region is real, what is even more real is the daily threat our colleagues and partners have been living under. We remain committed to supporting them as we work to restore operations and repair assets with a clear focus on safety and disciplined risk management. The Middle East is and will continue to be an advantaged and meaningful component of our global portfolio. The disruption to the broader economy we are seeing underscores the critical role our company plays in providing the affordable, reliable energy and products the world depends on. What we produce remains essential to development and progress, sustaining and improving living standards around the world. In this environment, scale, integration, and execution excellence matters. Those advantages, combined with the deep experience and capability of our employees, give us the ability to respond quickly and manage effectively through disruptions. Our competitive advantages are on display in this quarter's results. We delivered strong operational performance in a challenging environment, maintained rigorous safety and reliability standards, and continued advancing key priorities across the portfolio, supporting long-term value creation for our shareholders. We saw those advantages in our response to supply disruptions, leveraging our global portfolio to support customers. We delivered on our plans to increase Permian production year-over-year, achieved record levels of production in Guyana, achieved first LNG at Golden Pass, optimized logistics and crude product flows, and safely maximized refinery throughput where possible. In fact, in March, refinery throughput increased by approximately 200,000bbl a day versus February, or the equivalent of a mid-sized refinery. As we brought back refineries from turnaround and deferred maintenance activities where we could without impacting safety or long-term reliability. Our global supply chain organization rapidly executed alternate routings from the U.S. Gulf Coast to Asia to sustain critical supplies for our customers. Despite the unprecedented impacts in the global energy system, we maintained deliveries to our customers globally through coordinated planning and real-time vessel visibility. Financially, excluding identified items and estimated timing effects, our first quarter earnings per share were up versus the fourth quarter of 2025, reflecting the strength and resiliency of the underlying business. Stronger portfolio mix, structural cost reductions, and execution excellence continue to drive improving performance. Those same factors leave us better positioned to manage uncertainty versus several years ago. The strength of that advantage portfolio is clear in the work we're doing today. We are expanding our LNG footprint. Our newest facility, Golden Pass LNG, a joint venture with QatarEnergy, is increasing U.S. export capacity at an important moment for global supply. Train 1 of the facility achieved first LNG in March and will deliver an increase of about 5% relative to 2025 U.S. exports. By the time the third train is online, we will increase the country's current LNG exports by roughly 15%. At the same time, we continue to progress toward final investment decisions on LNG projects in Papua New Guinea and Mozambique, both expected later this year. Elsewhere in the upstream, Guyana continues to set the standard for execution, development pace, and value creation. We delivered record production, continued strong reliability, and have Uaru, Whiptail, and Hammerhead projects under construction, with Uaru expecting first oil late this year. Consistent with our broader approach to support long-term economic development in countries where we operate, we've committed a $100 million investment over 10 years to support national STEM education in Guyana, strengthening our bond with the people of Guyana and establishing a foundation for long-term prosperity. In the Permian, we continue to show how scale and proprietary technologies improve efficiency, recovery, and long-term value creation. We remain on track to grow full-year Permian production to 1.8 million oil equivalent barrels in 2026, with that growth grounded in value, not volume. We're also progressing our Permian net zero ambition with continuous methane monitoring implemented across all key assets in New Mexico. In product solutions, performance remains strong, driven by higher value products and technology-led differentiation. The Beaumont Refinery expansion, completed in 2023, fully recovered its initial investment ahead of expectation and is contributing to stronger margins and cash flow. This underscores how disciplined investments grounded in long-term market fundamentals rigorously executed generate durable returns independent of price cycles. In parallel, we continue to progress our journey to build a reliable domestic supply of advanced synthetic graphite. We recently held a ribbon-cutting ceremony at the pilot production plant in Kentucky, which represents a critical milestone between lab-scale development and full commercial deployment. In low-carbon solutions, we began transporting and storing captured CO2 from the New Generation Gas Gathering project, our second startup in less than a year. Through this year and next, we plan to start facilities with the capacity to capture an additional 4 million tons per year of CO2. Importantly, with our advantages, these projects deliver attractive returns that compete with the investments in our base business. Technology as a core competitive advantage remains central to our strategy, is one of the ways we improve structural competitiveness, strengthen returns, and create new earnings opportunity. In Guyana, we achieved the first deep water fully autonomous well section using rig automation and automated downhole steering tools, improving both safety and efficiency. Additionally, we're on track to leverage our Proxxima technology in subsea applications with Hammerhead and future FPSOs, further demonstrating the material's performance in demanding offshore environments. Across the company, we're making further progress to simplify how we run the business through effective application of technology. Our enterprise-wide process and data platform transformation, the largest ever undertaken in the industry, reached an important milestone with the successful launch of a new modern workforce enablement system. This significantly simplifies the work processes that underpin our talent management approach and streamlines our payroll processes in more than 50 countries. It provides a single, consistent data foundation on which future system deployments will be built. We deliver this with no business disruption, demonstrating the strength of our centralized core capabilities, fully leveraging our scale advantage. This is the first step of many to make our processes more efficient and effective, ultimately enhancing the experience of our global workforce. This will allow our people to focus their efforts on high-value work, further reinforcing our competitive advantages. Without the changes we made over the last decade and the focus we've put on leveraging our core advantages, this game-changing enterprise system would not be possible. It is establishing a truly differentiating foundation for long-term competitive advantage. With recent events, the world has been reminded of the critical role and long-term need for reliable, affordable Energy Products. Today, more people recognize that demand for oil and natural gas remains substantial and will continue to play an important role in global economic growth far into the future. This fundamental and the competitive advantages we bring underpin our strategy, our capital allocation decisions, and the long-term success of our company. We are confident in our advantages, the importance of scale and integration, the critical role of technology and execution excellence, and the power of talented people. We are confident in our continuing transformation and the critical role our company will play in any future scenario. We're confident in our plan to build long-term sustainable earnings and cash flow growth, the basis for long-term growth and shareholder value. Thank you. Jim ChapmanThank you, Darren. Before we move to Q&A, I want to highlight that we plan to publish our 2026 Advancing Climate Solutions report this month, detailing all of our progress on solving the and equation, meeting demand and reducing emissions, as well as our latest sustainability report. All these documents can be found on the investors section of our website. We really encourage you to take a look. With that, let's move to Q&A. Please note that we ask each analyst to limit themselves to one question as a courtesy to others. Operator, we'll ask you to please open the line for our first question. OperatorThank you. The question-and-answer session will be conducted electronically. If you'd like to ask a question, please do so by pressing the star key followed by the digit one on your telephone. The first question comes from Devin McDermott of Morgan Stanley. Devin McDermottHey, good morning. Thanks for taking my question. Devin McDermottDarren, good morning. I wanted to try to unpack some of your views on the near and longer-term impacts from the situation in the Middle East. That's, in this particular case, the reason we had as an identified item, is that with the disruption, the paper that we put in place for the physicals that we bought, the physicals weren't delivered, so we ended up with a naked hedge. That's, was basically a unique circumstance, given this, the disruptions here, that's what the identified item is. Neil, anything to add to that? Neil HansenYeah. Yeah, absolutely. Maybe to build on that a little bit, Darren. Again, this mismatch that occurs is the difference between the accounting standards that require us to value the financial derivatives based on the price that we see at the end of the period. As Darren mentioned, the physical transaction, the value of that remains on the balance sheet until the transaction's complete. What you see is in periods of rising prices, like we saw in the first quarter, these timing effects typically are negative. Then in times when we see decreasing prices, we see the opposite of that, and the timing effects become positive. I think importantly, as Darren mentioned, when you take aside these timing effects, the trading activity that we do, the optimization has consistently delivered positive earnings for the corporation. Good morning, and thanks for getting me on. Darren, you spent a lot of time on the hydrocarbon side of your business and global disruptions. Could you give us a little bit of an update on the power opportunities in the Gulf Coast? Thanks for the question, Nitin. I would tell you, I wanna make sure that kind of our objective in this space is clear, and I've said this when we first started talking about the data centers in this. The recognition of the growing demand here is we're not interested in the utility business of providing power. Because we don't think, ultimately that we bring, you know, a unique set of capabilities there that would manifest itself in above average industry returns. What we're interested in is bringing the unique capability and capacity to generate power with, you know, virtually carbon-free or emissions-free by using the decarbonized natural gas that we're producing and the unconventional business and our carbon capture and storage business and the leveraging the unique and frankly, only globally end-to-end supply chain or value chain for capturing, transporting, and sequestering CO2. That, for us, is the play here. As you know, we've been growing our carbon capture and storage business with third parties, establishing contracts to capture the CO2 and to transport and store it. The power side of the data centers is an opportunity to do that. To the extent these hyperscalers and the data centers wanna have very low emissions power, we have the option to provide that. We're in discussion with a number of hyperscalers. We're working through the specifics of the opportunity and the fiscals, and I would say that those are continuing dialogues. Frankly, it's a function of, you know, what the demand there is. I think what we, what we've seen in this whole low-carbon space, above and beyond carbon capture and storage, which is manifesting itself in real deals, that it's challenged when people, you know, are forced to, you know, pay for the emissions reductions when in many cases the market's not recognizing or rewarding it. That has been the challenge in this space, and we'll see in this particular area whether we overcome that challenge with customers and their desire to have low-carbon power. Jim ChapmanAll right. Shares of AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) slipped over 1% in overnight trading late Tuesday as the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) cleared Amazon’s $11.5 billion Globalstar acquisition, pushing the tech giant’s satellite-to-phone ambitions forward and setting the stage for tougher competition. ASTS stock jumped 6% on Tuesday to $41.96, but shares are still down 29% for the month. The FCC’s Space Bureau approved the transaction on Tuesday, including the transfer of 25 megahertz of Globalstar’s internationally harmonized mobile-satellite spectrum.  “This will enhance Amazon’s offering of direct-to-device (D2D) services, which will mean even more competition, coverage, and capacity,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said on X. The deal will pair Amazon Leo’s satellite-building capabilities, launch arrangements and ground infrastructure with Globalstar’s existing network and spectrum. The spectrum is key to Amazon’s satellite-to-phone ambitions. In its approval order, the FCC said Amazon has applied to operate a global direct-to-device system but would lack the mobile-satellite spectrum needed to run it without the acquisition. Amazon plans to use Globalstar’s assets to expand capacity and bring more services to areas beyond cellular coverage. The FCC said the deal could help close coverage gaps, boost emergency communications and improve data services for businesses and industrial users. “By approving this deal, the FCC has empowered Amazon Leo to deliver fast, next-gen satellite broadband services, increase competition, and help communities stay connected all across the country,” Carr said in the announcement. The FCC’s review also highlights how the deal could strengthen a rival to AST SpaceMobile. In its approval order, the agency cited arguments from Public Knowledge and New America’s Open Technology Institute that combining Amazon’s resources with Globalstar’s assets could create a stronger competitor to SpaceX and T-Mobile’s satellite offering, as well as AST’s partnership with AT&T. The order also notes AST’s ties with Verizon and FirstNet. AST already has FCC authorization to deploy and operate up to 248 satellites, connecting directly to standard smartphones using 700 MHz and 800 MHz spectrum in coordination with AT&T, Verizon and FirstNet. Its commercial agreement with AT&T, announced in 2024, runs through 2030. AST also signed a definitive agreement with Verizon last year. Amazon is targeting a similar opportunity: helping mobile carriers extend voice, text and data services beyond the reach of cellular towers. The company plans to begin deploying its next-generation satellite-to-device system in 2028. The deal would bring Amazon an established Apple relationship, with Globalstar already supporting emergency messaging and location sharing on compatible iPhones and Apple Watches. Amazon and Apple have agreed to maintain those services and develop future satellite features through Amazon Leo. Amazon also aims to expand beyond Globalstar’s current offerings to serve more carriers and device makers. The acquisition is expected to close in 2027, subject to remaining conditions, including replacement-satellite milestones. Amazon’s separate application for its direct-to-device system remains pending. After closing, it could also use Globalstar’s U.S. market-access approval for the planned 48-satellite C-3 network. Meanwhile, the FCC’s meeting on Thursday could advance a spectrum auction and proposals to open 500 megahertz of additional spectrum for uses including satellite-to-device services. (BA) stock is heading for a weekly loss as CEO Robert Ortberg outlined a path to $10 billion in free cash flow by 2029, with the company’s 737 production stabilization taking longer than expected. Boeing expects to reach its target production rate of 47 jets monthly in 2027, with cash flow improving over the next three years. Boeing stock edged up 0.2% overnight Tuesday after a 10% drop in regular trading. During the third-quarter (Q3) earnings call, Ortberg said Boeing is working to establish a manufacturing pace of 47 737 aircraft per month and needs additional time to sustain its targeted production rate. “On 737, we continue to work towards stabilizing production at 47 airplanes per month. Our factory key performance indicators are performing well, particularly in the final assembly, where we've seen a 40% improvement in rework since the start of last year. However, as I mentioned at a conference last month, it is taking us longer than we had expected to demonstrate performance at rate 47. We're making progress, but we still have more work to do, and I'm expecting it will take us into next year to get fully stable at this rate.” Boeing received U.S. approval last week for the 737 Max 10, its largest model in the 737 Max family, after a six-year wait. The plane has over 1,550 orders, making up more than 30% of Boeing’s total 737 Max orders. The delay followed safety checks after two deadly 737 Max 8 crashes in 2018 and 2019. Ortberg acknowledged that shareholders have struggled to predict how Boeing’s operational improvements would translate into the balance sheet. The company expects to generate roughly $2 billion in free cash flow in 2026, followed by approximately $3 billion in 2027. That 2027 outlook includes additional capital spending to develop the F/A-XX program, the U.S. Navy’s sixth-generation fighter jet contract. Boeing expects free cash flow to rise to about $6 billion in 2028 before reaching its $10 billion goal in 2029. Ortberg expects the financial recovery to pick up as some existing pressures ease. The 777X program will remain a drag in the near term. “With respect to program cash flow, we continue to expect 2027 to be a significant use of cash with 2028 improving before turning positive in 2029,” said CFO Jesus Malave of the 777X. Jefferies called Boeing’s free cash flow targets “disappointing,” noting that each year’s goal had slipped by about a year. In Q3, Boeing reported a loss of $0.34 per share, an improvement from a loss of $7.47 per share a year earlier but worse than analysts’ estimate of a loss of $0.25 per share, according to Fiscal.ai.
